summary:
The C2 failure collector retains one unambiguous final failing public verify command/input/owner tuple as exact bytes with sizes and hashes. Closed shapes, byte/frame/deadline limits, privacy checks, original exit and cleanup remain determining. Current owner receipts add a null or finite positive retirement deadline and strictly null detached-domain fields; legacy receipt scopes remain supported. Diagnostic retention and compiler output never grant retry or formal acceptance.

Unmodified upstream Quint0.32.0 drops the TLA compilation error explanation on its TLC verification path. The C2-only diagnostic derivative changes that one returned message while preserving structured errors, success/failure stage and exit. It has a distinct identity and actual produced byte hash, never the published canonical binary identity. Canonical Quint939b, C3/C5, model sources,150-second verify budgets, retry and retirement rules remain unchanged. Controlled actual CLI/gRPC old-RED/new-GREEN and isolated production-function controls run in the maintained producer before upload without a JVM/model checker; they do not reproduce or explain an earlier hosted compiler failure. Independent failed/successful hosted jobs retain their own outcomes.

The source-pinned builder declares the upstream archive/lock/patch, exact Node/npm/Deno and separate official denort runtime bytes, and an offline runtime dependency inventory. Cached-only JS resolution does not close the compiler-runtime input: Deno can separately fetch denort. A new private build root provisions the verified declared runtime before compile; ambient caches and workflow credentials are excluded from build children. Build-root bytes may enter the executable, so each actual trusted build records its own output hash rather than claiming cross-root or upstream byte reproduction.

Each existing workflow preparation job builds once and emits a separate sidecar. Only base consumers authenticate the current source/run/attempt1, producer job and its upload ID/digest, native ZIP digest and exact manifest/executable/license population before formal work. Current recipe, preflight and binary hashes are checked; a trusted consumer manifest-hash binding prevents recomputed local custody from admitting changed executables. Late reads, extraction, persistence and final build completion refuse a positive result. Malformed, changed, foreign or stale inputs block dependent work. The distinct C2 profile and complete source/manifest/custody pins survive owned-command/public-tuple reporting; coherent toolchain and harness identities bind the new inputs. This is a source preparation contract, not publication, profile activation, hosted formal success, native image acceptance or an explanation of the original compiler failure.
title: Retain complete public C2 diagnostic counterparts without granting retry authority
